nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.10@2026-08-24.body:
- To be granted a resident visa under the Skilled Migrant Category, all applicants must:
- meet health and character requirements for residence (see A4 and A5); and
- meet the applicable minimum standard of English or, where instructions allow, pre-purchase English for Speakers of other Languages (ESOL) tuition (see SR2.10).
- In addition, the principal applicant must:
- be aged 55 or younger at the time the residence application is made; and
- meet the skilled employment, pathway and skilled work experience requirements (as set out at (c) below) for one of the following Skilled Migrant Category pathways:
- Points-based pathway (column A); or
- Skilled Work Experience pathway (Column B); or
- Trades and Technician pathway (Column C).
- Overview of each pathway:
| | | Column A Points-based pathway SR3.25 6 points must be obtained from a skill category, or a combination of one skill category and skilled work experience in New Zealand. | Column B Skilled Work Experience pathway SR3.35 | Column C Trades and Technician pathway SR3.40

- Principal applicants applying via the Skilled Work Experience pathway, with skilled employment in an occupation listed in Appendix 21 (the Amber List) must meet the Amber List requirements.
- Principal applicants with skilled employment in an occupation listed in Appendix 22 (the Red List) may only apply via the Points-based pathway.
- Principal applicants must meet the SMC wage threshold (including any multiplier that applies to their chosen pathway and occupation) in effect at the time:
- they began to accrue the skilled work experience in New Zealand that counts towards meeting their pathway requirements at SR3.10(c); or
- they were invited to apply for residence (if no skilled work experience is required); or
- their work visa was granted, if it was granted in the five months before the applicant began to accrue their skilled work experience in New Zealand that counts towards meeting the requirements at SR3.10(c)(iii).
Example #1:
-An applicant applying via the Skilled Work Experience pathway (whose occupation is not on the Amber List).
-They need 2 years of skilled work experience in New Zealand, paid at 1.1 times the SMC wage threshold accrued in the 4 years prior to applying for their resident visa.
-They began their skilled work experience in New Zealand on 10 August 2023, in a role paying $33 per hour when the SMC wage threshold was $32.62.
-They must be paid more than $32.62 for both their skilled employment and skilled work experience in New Zealand, as long as they are invited to apply before 10 August 2027.
Example #2:
-An applicant is applying via the Points-based pathway and in an ANZSCO 1-3 role.
-They need 2 years of skilled work experience in New Zealand, paid at the SMC wage threshold accrued in the 4 years prior to applying for their resident visa.
-They had their work visa approved on 14 January 2023, when the SMC wage threshold was $27.76.
-They began their skilled work experience on 13 June 2023 in a role paying $28.00 per hour when the SMC wage threshold had increased to $29.66.
-However, as less than five months had passed between the date of visa approval and the commencement of their skilled employment, they are considered to meet the SMC wage threshold as long as they maintain at or above the wage threshold in effect on 14 January 2023 and as long as they are invited to apply before 13 June 2027.
- Despite (f), applicants claiming 6 points from one skill category and with skilled employment that is a contract for services must meet the wage threshold (including any multipliers) (SR3.10.5.1):
- in effect at the time they began their skilled work experience in New Zealand that counts towards their experience as a contractor; and
- the wage threshold in effect at the time they are invited to apply for residence for their skilled employment
- An applicant may be considered to meet the SMC wage threshold relevant to them if they meet the wage thresholds that were the basis for them being invited to apply for residence.
- For the purpose of determining whether skilled work experience has been completed within the eligible period, the eligible period is calculated backwards from the date the resident visa application is submitted.
Example:
-An applicant is applying via the Skilled work experience pathway, in an occupation that is not on the Amber List.
-They need 2 years of skilled work experience, paid at 1.1 times the SMC wage threshold, accrued in the 4 years prior to applying for their resident visa.
-They had their work visa granted on the 14 June 2022 and began their skilled work experience on 14 January 2023, as such the grace period of 5 months does not apply.
-They submitted their expression of interest 13 January 2027 (within the 4 year skilled work experience window) and submitted their resident visa application on 14 March 2027 (within the 4-month ITA period).
-At EOI, they were able to use the SMC wage threshold in effect on the date they began to accrue their skilled work experience (going back up to 4 years), in this example they can use the SMC wage threshold in effect on 14 January 2023.
-However, skilled work experience must be accrued in the 4 years prior to resident visa application so only work experience completed from 14 March 2023 will be counted (as it must be completed within 48 months prior to submitting their residence application on 14 March 2027).
- Despite R5.7, where the Skilled Migrant Category instructions under SR2 refer to ANZSCO, any assessment must be based on the immigration view of version 1.3 of the ANZSCO.
Note:
-The Immigration view of version 1.3 of the ANZSCO provided by Statistics New Zealand is available here: Aria Stats NZ - ANZSCO

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.15.5@2026-08-24.body:
- An applicant will be assessed as being suitably qualified if they:
- have a relevant qualification meeting the requirements at SR3.25.5(b) that is at, or above, the qualification level on the New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework (NZQCF) that corresponds to the indicative skill level described for their occupation in the ANZSCO; or
- have the relevant work experience that the ANZSCO indicates may substitute for the required qualification; or
- are in a skill level 1 occupation and have five years of relevant work experience; or
- are in a skill level 2 or 3 occupation and have three years of relevant work experience; or
- have current registration for their employment listed at SR3.30 or Appendix 16.
- Qualifications are relevant to employment if the major subject area of the principal applicant's recognised qualification is directly applicable to the employment, or an immigration officer is satisfied that the qualification was a key factor in the employer's decision to employ the principal applicant in that position.
- Work experience is relevant to employment if the employer considers, and an immigration officer is satisfied, that the work experience is directly applicable to the employment, or the offer of employment could not reasonably have been made, or the employment could not reasonably have been undertaken, if the principal applicant did not have that work experience.
- Where their skilled employment is in an occupation that requires registration by law (see Appendix 16), the principal applicant must have the required full or provisional registration for that occupation in New Zealand (or a letter of eligibility from the New Zealand Medical or Dental Council) to be suitably qualified.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.15.5@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.15 Skilled employment / SR3.15.5 Suitably qualified

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.15@2026-08-24.body:
- The principal applicant’s employment or offer of employment must be:
- full-time (employment is full-time if it amounts to at least 30 guaranteed hours per week for every week worked); and
- with an employer who is accredited (and their accreditation is not suspended) at the time the residence application is either made or decided; and
- permanent or for a fixed term of at least 12 months; and
- genuine and not offered as the result of payment (see SR2.1.5).
- A contract for services will be acceptable where:
- the principal applicant meets the requirements for at least 12 months of skilled work experience in New Zealand (see SR3.20); and
- the principal applicant has a consistent history of contract work; and
- the principal applicant has a current contract or contracts totalling at least 6 months duration; and
- an immigration officer is satisfied that such contract work is likely to be sustained.
- As evidence of their current employment or offer of employment, applicants must provide an employment agreement and job description specifying the name of the applicant, name of employer (their legal entity), occupation, hours and remuneration of the employment.
- For independent midwife practitioners, a letter of authority to claim under the Maternity Notice pursuant to section 94 of the Pae Ora (Healthy Futures) Act 2022, and evidence of registration with the Midwifery Council is sufficient to meet the requirements at SR3.15(a)(i) and (iii), and SR3.15(b)(ii) to (iv).
- Applicants must also meet any pathway-specific skilled employment requirements as listed at:
- SR3.25.1 for the Points-based pathway; or
- SR3.35.1 for the Skilled Work Experience pathway; or
- SR3.40.1 for the Trades and Technician pathway.

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.1@2023-10-09.body: The objective of the Skilled Migrant Category is to support New Zealand’s economic growth by providing for the grant of resident visas to people who demonstrate they can fill medium to long term skill needs in New Zealand.

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.20@2025-08-18.body:
- The principal applicant must have current employment or an offer of employment in New Zealand that pays at least the equivalent of:
- the median wage (currently $33.56 per hour) if their occupation is listed at ANZSCO skill level 1-3; or
- 1.5 times the median wage (currently $50.34 per hour) if their occupation listed at ANZSCO skill level 4-5, or not included in the ANZSCO.
Note: The median wage rate of $33.56 for the Skilled Migrant Category reflects the June 2024 publication of median wage data by Statistics New Zealand.
- The principal applicant’s employment or offer of employment must be:
- full-time (employment is full-time if it amounts to at least 30 guaranteed hours per week for every week worked); and
- with an employer who is accredited (and their accreditation is not suspended) at the time the residence application is either made or decided; and
- permanent or for a fixed term of at least 12 months; and
- genuine and not offered as the result of payment (see SR2.1.5); and
- A contract for services will be acceptable where:
- the applicant meets the requirements for at least 12 months of skilled work experience in New Zealand (see SR3.35); and
- the applicant has a consistent history of contract work; and
- the applicant has a current contract or contracts totalling at least 6 months duration; and
- an immigration officer is satisfied that such contract work is likely to be sustained.
- As evidence of current skilled employment, applicants must provide an employment agreement and job description specifying the occupation, hours and remuneration of the employment.
- For independent midwife practitioners, a letter of authority to claim under the Maternity Notice pursuant to section 94 of the Pae Ora (Healthy Futures) Act 2022, and evidence of registration with the Midwifery Council is sufficient to meet the requirements at SR3.20(b)(i) and (iii), and SR3.20(c)(ii) to (iv).
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.20@2025-08-18.heading: SR3.20 Skilled employment

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.20@2026-08-24.body:
- Skilled work experience in New Zealand is time that the applicant worked in full-time employment (employment is full-time if it amounts to at least 30 hours per week for every week worked) in New Zealand where they earned at least the equivalent of the SMC wage threshold required by their chosen pathway.
- The SMC wage threshold in effect over time (including any applicable multiplier) is specified in SR3.10.5
- Skilled work experience must have been lawfully obtained and will not be counted if the principal applicant was unlawfully in New Zealand or required authority to undertake employment but did not have such authority.
- The principal applicant’s employment during skilled work experience in New Zealand must be genuine and not offered as the result of payment (see SR2.1.5).
- For skilled work experience in New Zealand, work on a contract for services is acceptable.
- As evidence of skilled work experience in New Zealand, applicants must provide:
- employment agreements and job descriptions (previous and current), specifying the name of the applicant, name of the employer (their legal entity), the occupation, hours and remuneration of any employment; and
- a summary of earnings or a tax statement (for work on a contract for services) from the Inland Revenue confirming the period of work and income over any period of work.
- Principal applicants must also meet any pathway-specific skilled work experience in New Zealand requirements as listed at:
- SR3.25.25 for the Points-based pathway; or
- SR3.35.5.5 for the Skilled Work Experience pathway; or
- SR3.40.10.5 for the Trades and Technician pathway.
Note: Skilled work experience in New Zealand does not have to be completed consecutively and can be a total of different periods, for example two 12-month periods with a gap of six months in between to make up a 24-month period.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.20@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.20 Skilled work experience in New Zealand

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.25.10@2026-08-24.body:

- As evidence of income, applicants must provide an employment agreement and job description specifying the name of the applicant, name of the employer (their legal entity), occupation, hours and remuneration of the employment.
- For the avoidance of doubt, where an applicant is applying via the points-based pathway and is claiming points for income, the SMC wage threshold for any skilled work experience must also meet the applicable multiplier.

-As the applicant began working within 5 months of their work visa grant date, the SMC wage threshold in effect on 12 December 2024 applies.
-Two times the SMC wage threshold on that date was $63.22.

- a level 9 qualification to qualify for 4 points; or
- a level 8 qualification to qualify for 3 points.

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.25.1@2026-08-24.body:
Principal applicants applying via the Points-based pathway must have current employment, or an offer of employment, in New Zealand that pays at least the equivalent of:
- the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5) if their occupation is listed at ANZSCO skill level 1-3; or
- 1.5 times the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5) if their occupation is listed at ANZSCO skill level 4-5 or not included in ANZSCO.

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.25.1@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.25 Points-based pathway / SR3.25.1 Skilled employment for the Points based pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.25.25@2026-08-24.body:
- To qualify for points from skilled work experience, principal applicants applying via the Points-based pathway must complete skilled work experience in New Zealand, prior to submitting the residence application, for:
- 2 years in the prior 4 years to qualify for 3 points; or
- 1 year and 6 months in the prior 3 years to qualify for 2 points; or
- 1 year in the prior 2 years to qualify for 1 point.
- Applicants claiming 6 points from one points-based skilled category (SR3.25.5) and holding contracts for services for their skilled employment must complete 1 year of skilled work experience in New Zealand, in the 2 years prior to submitting the residence instructions.
- Skilled work experience must be paid at least:
- the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5) if the occupation for their skilled work experience is listed at ANZSCO skill level 1-3; or
- 1.5 times the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5) if the occupation for their skilled work experience is listed at ANZSCO skill level 4-5 or not included in ANZSCO; or
- the wage required by SR3.25.10 if they are claiming points for income.
Note: The SMC wage threshold in effect over time (including any applicable multiplier) can be found in SR3.10.5, to determine the date that applies, refer to SR3.10(f).
Example: If an applicant began working in a role paying $28.00 per hour on 14 January 2023 when the SMC wage threshold was $27.76 and they need to accrue 2 years of work experience in the 4 years prior to their SMC application, provided they maintain this rate, and they are invited to apply for residence under SMC before 13 January 2027, they will be considered to meet the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5).
- Applicants claiming points for recognised New Zealand registration, licensing, or certification, must complete their skilled work experience in New Zealand after gaining that registration, license, or certification.
- Where an applicant’s skilled work experience was obtained in an ANZSCO skill level 4–5 role, but their offer of employment, is in an ANZSCO skill level 1–3 role (or vice versa), their relevant SMC wage is the rate in effect on the date they began to accrue skilled work experience in New Zealand (see SR3.10.5).
- Where an applicant has periods of skilled work experience in occupations at different skill levels (i.e. ANZSCO skill levels 1–3 and ANZSCO skill levels 4–5), each period of skilled work experience must meet the relevant multiplier of the SMC wage threshold that was in effect on the date the applicant began to accrue skilled work experience.
Example:
-Applicant has 5 points from registration and needs 1 point from 1 year of skilled work experience in New Zealand
-The applicant’s skilled work experience was in an ANZSCO skill level 4-5 role
-They began their skilled work experience on 10 August 2025 when 1.5 times SMC wage threshold was $47.41
-For their skilled work experience in New Zealand, they must have been paid at or above $47.41
-Now they are applying for SMC, their skilled employment is in an ANZSCO 1-3 role
-ANZSCO 1-3 roles must be paid the SMC wage threshold
-The SMC wage threshold on the date they began to accrue their skilled work experience in New Zealand was $31.61
-As such, the applicant must be paid at or above $31.61 for their skilled employment.

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.30@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.30 Points for New Zealand registration, licensing, or certification

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35.1@2026-08-24.body:
- Principal applicants applying via the Skilled Work Experience pathway must have current employment, or an offer of employment, in New Zealand that:
- is in an occupation listed at ANZSCO skill level 1-3, that is not listed in Appendix 22 (The Red List); and either
- pays at least 1.1 times the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5); or
- pays at least 1.2 times the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5) if the occupation is listed in Appendix 21 (The Amber List).
Note: The SMC wage threshold in effect over time (including any applicable multiplier) can be found in SR3.10.5, to determine the date that applies, refer to SR3.10(f).
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35.1@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.35 Skilled Work Experience Pathway / SR3.35.1 Skilled employment for the Skilled Work Experience pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35.5.1@2026-08-24.body:
- Directly relevant work experience must be:
- full-time (employment is full-time if it amounts to at least 30 hours per week for every week worked); and
- in an occupation listed at ANZSCO skill level 1-3; and
- directly relevant to the offer of skilled employment; and
- completed in the 10 years immediately prior to submitting the current residence application.
- Work experience must not be self-employment.
- Directly relevant work experience can be accrued in any country (including New Zealand), unless the applicant’s skilled employment is in an occupation in Appendix 21 (The Amber List), in which case, it must be accrued in New Zealand.
- As evidence of work experience, applicants must provide:
- an employment agreement or an employment contract or a service agreement (previous and current), and job description specifying the name of the applicant, name of the employer (their legal entity), occupation, hours and remuneration of any employment; and
- a summary of earnings or a tax statement confirming the period of work and income over any period of work or (for overseas work experience only) a certificate of service.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35.5.1@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.35 Skilled Work Experience Pathway / SR3.35.5.1 Directly relevant work experience requirements for the Skilled Work Experience pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35.5.5@2026-08-24.body:
- Skilled work experience in New Zealand for the Skilled Work Experience pathway must be:
- directly relevant to the offer of employment or skilled employment; and
- completed within the 4 years prior to submitting the residence application; and either
- paid at least 1.1 times the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5) unless (iv) below applies; or
- paid at least 1.2 times the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5) for occupations listed in Appendix 21 (The Amber List).
Note: The SMC wage threshold in effect over time (including any applicable multiplier) can be found in SR3.10.5, to determine the date that applies, refer to SR3.10(f).
Example: If an applicant began working in a role paying $31.00 per hour on 14 January 2023, when 1.1 times the SMC wage threshold was $30.53, and they need to accrue 2 years of work experience in the 4 years prior to their SMC application, they will meet the SMC wage threshold provided they maintain a pay rate of over $30.53 and are invited to apply for their resident visa before 13 January 2027 (see SR3.10.5).
Note: Skilled work experience is considered to be directly relevant to the offer of employment if it meets SR3.35.10(c).
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35.5.5@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.35 Skilled Work Experience Pathway / SR3.35.5.5 Skilled work experience in New Zealand for the Skilled Work Experience pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35.5@2026-08-24.body:
- Principal applicants applying via the Skilled Work Experience pathway must demonstrate that they have at least a total of 5 years of work experience, including:
- at least 3 years of directly relevant work experience (see SR3.35.5.1); and
- at least an additional 2 years of skilled work experience in New Zealand (see SR3.35.5.5).
- Skilled work experience must be in an ANZSCO skill level 1-3 role.
- The same time period cannot be counted for both directly relevant (SR3.35.5.1) and skilled work experience in New Zealand (SR3.35.5.5).
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35.5@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.35 Skilled Work Experience Pathway / SR3.35.5 Work experience requirements for the Skilled Work Experience pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35@2025-08-18.body:
- When claiming points for skilled work experience in New Zealand, immediately prior to submitting the residence application, the principal applicant must have completed skilled work experience in New Zealand for:
- 36 months in the prior 60 months to qualify for 3 points; or
- 24 months in the prior 48 months to qualify for 2 points; or
- 12 months in the prior 24 months to qualify for 1 point.
Note: Skilled work experience in New Zealand does not have to be completed consecutively and can be a total of different periods, for example two 12-month periods with a gap of six months in between.
- Skilled work experience in New Zealand is time that the applicant worked in full-time employment (employment is full-time if it amounts to at least 30 guaranteed hours per week for every week worked) in New Zealand where they earned at least the equivalent of:
- the median wage if their occupation is listed at ANZSCO skill level 1-3; or
- 1.5 times the median wage if their occupation is listed at ANZSCO skill level 4-5, or not included in ANZSCO; or
- the wage required by SR3.25.1 if they have claimed points for income.
- The median wage in effect for the Skilled Migrant Category across time is:
| Date range | Median wage | 1.5 times median wage | 2 times median wage
| 15 January 2018 – 25 November 2018 | $24.29 | $36.44 | $48.58
| 26 November 2018 – 23 February 2020 | $25.00 | $37.50 | $50.00
| 24 February 2020 – 18 July 2021 | $25.50 | $38.25 | $51.00
| 19 July 2021 – 23 October 2022 | $27.00 | $40.50 | $54.00
| 24 October 2022 – 26 February 2023 | $27.76 | $41.64 | $55.52
| 27 February 2023 - 27 February 2024 | $29.66 | $44.49 | $59.32
| 28 February 2024 – 17 August 2025 | $31.61 | $47.41 | $63.22
| From 18 August 2025 | $33.56 | $50.34 | $67.12
- For applicants claiming points for New Zealand registration, licensing or certification, skilled work experience in New Zealand must have been completed after gaining that registration, license or certification.
- Skilled work experience must have been lawfully obtained and will not be counted if the principal applicant was unlawfully in New Zealand or required authority to undertake employment but did not have such authority.
- The principal applicant’s employment during skilled work experience in New Zealand must be genuine and not offered as the result of payment (see SR2.1.5).
- For skilled work experience in New Zealand, work on a contract for services is acceptable.
- As evidence of skilled work experience in New Zealand, applicants must provide:
- employment agreements and job descriptions (previous and current), specifying the occupation, hours and remuneration of any employment; and
- a summary of earnings or tax statement (for work on a contract for services) from the Inland Revenue confirming the period of work and income over any period of work.
- Despite SR3.35(b)(iii), for applicants claiming points for income of at least 2 times the median wage, skilled work experience in New Zealand is also acceptable if it was completed:
- on or after 29 September 2021 and before 9 October 2023; and
- in an occupation listed in Tier 2 of Appendix 13 while meeting the requirements listed in Tier 2 of Appendix 13 for that occupation.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.35@2025-08-18.heading: SR3.35 Skilled work experience in New Zealand

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.10.1@2026-08-24.body:

- in an occupation listed at ANZSCO skill level 1-3; and
- directly relevant to the offer of skilled employment; and
- completed in the 10 years immediately prior to submitting their residence application; and
- Directly relevant work experience can be accrued in any country (including New Zealand).
- Work experience must not be self-employment.
- As evidence of work experience applicants must provide:
- An employment agreement or an employment contract or a service agreement (previous and current), and job description specifying the name of the applicant, name of the employer (their legal entity), occupation, hours and remuneration of any employment; and

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.10.1@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.40 Trades and Technician Pathway / SR3.40.10.1 Directly relevant work experience requirements for the Trades and Technician pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.10.5@2026-08-24.body:
- Skilled work experience in New Zealand for the Trades and Technician pathway must be:
- paid at least the equivalent of the SMC wage threshold; and
- directly relevant to the offer of employment or skilled employment; and
- completed within the 3 years prior to submitting the residence application; and
- in an occupation listed at ANZSCO skill level 1-3.
Example: If an applicant began working in a role paying $30.00 per hour on 14 January 2024 when the SMC wage threshold was $29.66 and they need to accrue 18 months of work experience in the 36 months prior to their SMC application, if they maintain a rate of over $29.66 they will be considered to meet the SMC wage threshold as long as they apply for their resident visa before 13 January 2027 (see SR3.10.5 for the SMC wage threshold in effect across time).
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.10.5@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.40 Trades and Technician Pathway / SR3.40.10.5 Skilled work experience in New Zealand for the Trades and Technician pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.10@2026-08-24.body:
- Principal applicants applying via the Trades and Technician pathway must have a total of 4 years work experience, including:
- at least 2 years and 6 months of relevant work experience accrued from any country (including New Zealand); and
- at least an additional 18 months of skilled work experience accrued in New Zealand.
- The same time period cannot be counted for both relevant (SR3.40.10.1) and skilled work experience in New Zealand (SR3.40.10.5).
- All work experience must be accrued after receiving their relevant level 4 (or above) trade qualification (SR3.40.5).
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.10@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.40 Trades and Technician Pathway / SR3.40.10 Work Experience for the Trades and Technician pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.15@2026-08-24.body:
- In determining the ANZSCO skill level of an applicant’s work experience an immigration officer:
- will determine whether the applicant’s employment is substantially consistent with the ANZSCO occupation (6-digit) level job title and description for that occupation; and
- may undertake a substantial match assessment (see SR2.1.1).
- If an immigration officer is unable to determine a claimed substantial match to an ANZSCO occupation, they may request evidence of the tasks associated with that employment to assess whether the previous employment displays the characteristics of that occupation in terms of the relevant ANZSCO ‘Unit Group’ (4-digit) level description of tasks for that role.
- For applicants applying via the Trades and Technician pathway, work experience will only begin to be counted after the relevant qualification has been received.
- Work experience is directly relevant to employment if the employer considers, and an immigration officer is satisfied, that the work experience is directly applicable to the employment, or the offer of employment could not reasonably have been made, or the employment could not reasonably have been undertaken, if the principal applicant did not have that work experience.
- An applicant is eligible for the Trades and Technician pathway if their occupation was listed in Appendix 23 at the time the applicant began accruing their skilled work experience in New Zealand, even if the occupation was subsequently removed.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.15@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.40 Trades and Technician Pathway / SR3.40.15 Determining work experience for the Trades and Technician pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.1@2026-08-24.body:
Principal applicants applying via the Trades and Technician pathway must have current employment, or an offer of employment, in New Zealand that:
- is in an occupation listed in Appendix 23; and
- pays at least the equivalent of the SMC wage threshold (see SR3.10.5).
Note: The SMC wage threshold in effect over time (including any applicable multiplier) can be found in SR3.10.5, to determine the date that applies, refer to SR3.10(f).
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.40.1@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.40 Trades and Technician Pathway / SR3.40.1 Skilled employment for the Trades and Technician pathway

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.5.10@2026-08-24.body:
Applicants for a visa under the Skilled Migrant Category may only apply if:
- they have been invited to apply under the Skilled Migrant Category SR3 instructions; and
- they make their application within 4 months of the date that invitation is made; and
- they apply under the pathway they were invited to apply under; and
- their invitation has not been revoked.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.5.10@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.5 Applying for a Skilled Migrant Category Visa / SR3.5.10 Making an application

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.5.15@2026-08-24.body: Applications made on and after 24 August 2026 in response to an Invitation to Apply issued prior to 24 August 2026, will be assessed according to the Skilled Migrant Category (SR3) instructions and associated appendices in effect on 23 August 2026.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.5.15@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.5 Applying for a Skilled Migrant Category Visa / SR3.5.15 Invitation to Apply issued prior to 24 August 2026

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.5.1@2026-08-24.body:
- A person who is interested in applying for a resident visa under the Skilled Migrant Category must complete an expression of interest (EOI) form in the prescribed manner.
- An automated electronic system may determine whether an applicant meets the requirements to be invited to apply under the Skilled Migrant Category.
- An automated electronic system may issue or refuse to issue an invitation to apply under these instructions based on the claims made in a person’s EOI and set out in SR3.5.1(e) below.
- Where a decision to issue or refuse to issue an invitation to apply for a visa is made by way of an automated electronic system, that decision must for all purposes be treated as a decision of an immigration officer who is authorised to make the decision under the Immigration Act 2009.
- A person may only be invited to apply for a resident visa under the Skilled Migrant Category if the person expressing interest has:
- confirmed that they are aged 55 or younger; and
- confirmed that none of the people included in the EOI are described in sections 15 or 16 of the Immigration Act 2009 (see A5.20) concerning character; and
- confirmed that none of the people included in the EOI would be ineligible for a medical waiver (see A4.60); and
- confirmed that all people included in the EOI meet the minimum standard of English or, where instructions allow, intend to pre-purchase English for Speakers of Other Languages tuition (see SR2.10); and
- confirmed they meet the skilled employment requirements (see SR3.20); and either
- claimed they meet the pathway requirements for their chosen pathway (see SR3.10); and
- claimed they meet the skilled work experience in New Zealand requirements (if applicable) for their chosen pathway (see SR3.10).
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR3.5.1@2026-08-24.heading: SR3.5 Applying for a Skilled Migrant Category Visa / SR3.5.1 Ability to apply

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.10@2023-02-27.body:
Acceptable employment in a highly paid role is employment where the immigration officer is satisfied that the principal applicant:
- holds current employment or an offer of employment with remuneration of at least twice the median wage rate that is in effect at the beginning of the 24 month period and at the time the residence application is made (currently $59.32 per hour), and
- the employment or offer of employment is with an employer who is accredited at the time of the residence application (whose accreditation is not suspended); and
- the employment is full-time (employment is full-time if it amounts to at least 30 guaranteed hours per week for every week worked); and
- the employment is permanent or for a fixed term of at least 12 months from the date of application; and
- the employment is genuine and is not offered as a result of payment (see SM6.30.5 (a)).
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.10@2023-02-27.heading: SR4.10 Acceptable employment in a Skilled Residence: Highly Paid role

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.10@2024-02-28.body:
- Acceptable employment in a Tier 1 Green List occupation is employment where the immigration officer is satisfied that:
- the principal applicant holds current employment or an offer of employment for an occupation listed in Tier 1 of Appendix 13; and
- the requirements of that occupation specified in Tier 1 of Appendix 13 are met; and
- the remuneration for the employment or offer of employment is either:
- at or above the hourly rate specified in Tier 1 of Appendix 13 where an occupation has remuneration requirements; or
- at or above the median wage of $31.61; and
- the employment or offer of employment is with an employer who is accredited (and their accreditation is not suspended) at the time the residence application is either made or decided; and
- the employment is full-time (employment is full-time if it amounts to at least 30 guaranteed hours per week for every week worked); and
- the employment is permanent or for a fixed term of at least 12 months from when the application is made; and
- the employment is genuine and is not offered as a result of payment (see SR2.1.5).
- For the purpose of the acceptable employment instructions, a contract for services will be considered acceptable employment:
- where the applicant has a current contract or contracts for services totalling at least 6 months duration; and
- where a wage threshold and relevant work experience is specified for an occupation in Tier 1 of Appendix 13, the applicant meets the requirements specified for contract for service arrangements for that occupation.
- For independent midwife practitioners, a letter of authority to claim under the Maternity Notice pursuant to section 94 of the Pae Ora (Healthy Futures) Act 2022 and evidence of registration with the Midwifery Council is sufficient to meet the requirements at (b)(i).
- For roles that do not require occupational registration, an immigration officer may be required to assess whether the employment matches the Green List occupation. In determining whether employment is for a role on the Green List an immigration officer may undertake a substantial match assessment (see SR2.1.1).
Notes:
- The median wage of $31.61 for Green List Tier 1 reflects the June 2023 publication of median wage data by Statistics New Zealand.
- For the purposes of undertaking a substantial match assessment, immigration officers must make an assessment based on Version 1.2 of the ANZSCO is available at www.immigration.govt.nz/anzsco.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.10@2024-02-28.heading: SR4.10 Acceptable employment in a Tier 1 Green List role

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.10@2026-03-09.body:
- Acceptable employment in a Tier 1 Green List occupation is employment where the immigration officer is satisfied that:
- the principal applicant holds current employment or an offer of employment for an occupation listed in Tier 1 of Appendix 13; and
- the requirements of that occupation specified in Tier 1 of Appendix 13 are met; and
- the remuneration for the employment or offer of employment is either:
- at or above the hourly rate specified in Tier 1 of Appendix 13 where an occupation has remuneration requirements; or
- at or above the median wage of $35.00; and
- the employment or offer of employment is with an employer who is accredited (and their accreditation is not suspended) at the time the residence application is either made or decided; and
- the employment is full-time (employment is full-time if it amounts to at least 30 guaranteed hours per week for every week worked); and
- the employment is permanent or for a fixed term of at least 12 months from when the application is made; and
- the employment is genuine and is not offered as a result of payment (see SR2.1.5).
- For the purpose of the acceptable employment instructions, a contract for services will be considered acceptable employment:
- where the applicant has a current contract or contracts for services totalling at least 6 months duration; and
- where a wage threshold and relevant work experience is specified for an occupation in Tier 1 of Appendix 13, the applicant meets the requirements specified for contract for service arrangements for that occupation.
- For independent midwife practitioners, a letter of authority to claim under the Maternity Notice pursuant to section 94 of the Pae Ora (Healthy Futures) Act 2022 and evidence of registration with the Midwifery Council is sufficient to meet the requirements at (b)(i).
- For roles that do not require occupational registration, an immigration officer may be required to assess whether the employment matches the Green List occupation. In determining whether employment is for a role on the Green List an immigration officer may undertake a substantial match assessment (see SR2.1.1).
Notes:
- The median wage of $35.00 for Green List Tier 1 reflects the June 2025 publication of median wage data by Statistics New Zealand.
- For the purposes of undertaking a substantial match assessment, immigration officers must make an assessment based on Version 1.2 of the ANZSCO is available at www.immigration.govt.nz/anzsco.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.10@2026-03-09.heading: SR4.10 Acceptable employment in a Tier 1 Green List role

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.15@2023-02-27.body:
- Applicants must have worked for at least 24 months in a role on and after 29 September 2021 with remuneration of at least twice the median wage.
- Evidence that the applicant has earned twice the median wage can be demonstrated by:
- an employment agreement specifying their remuneration is at least twice the median wage; or
- a letter from the employer specifying their remuneration is at least twice the median wage; and
- a summary of earnings from Inland Revenue.
- The period of work in New Zealand must have been completed while the applicant was holding an Accredited Employer work visa. an interim visa granted while the applicant held an Accredited Employer work visa and had applied for a further Accredited Employer work visa.
- Despite (c) above, applicants who held or had applied for one of the following visas before 4 July 2022 and were earning twice the median wage while in full-time employment (at least 30 hours per week) can count their work (from 29 September 2021) towards the 24 month period:any work visa; or
- a critical purpose visitor visa with work conditions.
Note: With the exception of an accredited employer work visa, work on any work visa applied for on or after 4 July 2022 cannot be counted towards meeting the 24 month period.
- The 24 months of work must be gained during the 30 month period immediately before the date the residence application is made.
- Highly paid work will start to be counted when the applicant’s remuneration reaches at least twice the median hourly rate in place at that time as specified in the immigration instructions (provided they hold a visa described in (c) or (d) above).
- Work gained while earning at least twice the median wage will stop being counted if:
- the applicant ceases to hold one of the visas listed in (c) or (d) above, or
- the applicant’s remuneration decreases and the new rate is below twice the median wage.
- A table showing the twice the median wage rates in effect across time appears below
| Date range | Twice median hourly rate
| 29 September 2021 – 3 July 2022 | $54.00
| 4 July 2022 – 26 February 2023 | $55.52
| 27 February 2023-February 2024 | $59.32
- For the purposes of these instructions, any parental leave taken can be counted towards meeting the acceptable work in New Zealand requirements.
- If an applicant has worked in New Zealand for at least 24 months in the last 30 month period but has not maintained a salary at twice the median wage for the full 24 months, they can still been considered for the grant of residence if they meet the acceptable work requirements set out for the Work to Residence visa (SR3.15) for the balance of the 24 months.
Note: The 24 months of work in New Zealand does not have to be completed consecutively and can be a total of different periods, for example two 12-month periods with a gap of six months between. Additionally, it can be made up of different types of work in New Zealand, for example 6 months in a Tier 2 Green List role and 18 months in a role paid twice the median wage.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.15@2023-02-27.heading: SR4.15 Skilled Residence: Highly Paid requirements for 24 months of work in New Zealand

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.1@2022-09-05.body: The objective of the Skilled Residence: Highly Paid sub-category is to provide for the grant of resident visas to people who demonstrate they have been highly paid while working in New Zealand for 24 months.
nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.1@2022-09-05.heading: SR4.1 Skilled Residence: Highly Paid objective

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR4.5.1@2023-10-09.body:
- To demonstrate meeting specified evidential requirements for a Green List occupation (see Appendix 13) the applicant can provide the following:
- Qualification – the qualification and, if the Green List requirement is for a New Zealand qualification and the qualification is from outside New Zealand, an International Qualification Assessment (IQA) from the New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA).
Note: An IQA:
- assesses an overseas qualification (or group of qualifications) by stating the learning outcomes of the closest New Zealand equivalent qualification; and
- states the NZQF level and qualification type of that equivalent qualification; and
- refers to any verification of the applicant's qualifications undertaken by the NZQA.
- Registration or Professional Membership - documentation confirming registration or professional membership.
- Acceptable employment in a specified occupation - employment agreement and job description specifying the occupation.

- the remuneration for the employment or offer of employment is either:

- at or above the median wage of $31.61; and
- the employment or offer of employment is with an employer who is accredited (and their accreditation is not suspended) at the time the residence application is either made or decided; and
- the employment is full-time (employment is full-time if it amounts to at least 30 guaranteed hours per week for every week worked); and
- the employment is permanent or for a fixed term of at least 12 months from when the application is made; and
- the employment is genuine and is not offered as a result of payment (see SR2.1.5).

nz-inz-opsmanual:SR5.15@2024-02-28.body:
- Applicants must have worked for at least 24 months in New Zealand in an occupation on Tier 2 of the Green List, on and after 29 September 2021.
- To be considered as having worked in a Tier 2 Green List occupation, applicants must have met the requirements for their occupation as specified in the Green List for the duration of the 24 month period.
- For the 24 months of work in New Zealand, applicants must have been working full-time (at least 30 hours a week) in a Tier 2 Green List occupation and held one of the following visas:
- any work visa; or
- a critical purpose visitor visa with work conditions; or
- an interim visa granted while the applicant held a work visa or a critical purpose visitor visa with work conditions and had applied for a further work visa.
- The 24 months of work must be gained during the 30-month period immediately before the date the residence application is made.
- Where an occupation has remuneration requirements, the work period will start to be counted when the applicant’s remuneration reaches the hourly rate specified in Tier 2 of Appendix 13 for that occupation at that time (provided they hold a visa described in (c) above).
- Where an occupation does not have remuneration requirements, the work period will start to be counted when the applicant’s remuneration is at or above the median wage at that time (SR5.15.1) (provided they hold a visa described in (c) above).
- The work period (while earning the specified hourly rate) will stop being counted if:
- the applicant ceases to hold one of the visas listed in (c) above; or
- the applicant changes employment and their new income is below:
- the median wage (SR5.15.1) at that time; or
- the hourly rate specified in Tier 2 of Appendix 13 for that occupation at that time; or
- the applicant’s remuneration decreases, and the new rate is below:
- the median wage (SR5.15.1) at that time; or
- the hourly rate specified in Tier 2 of Appendix 13 for that occupation at that time.
- A table showing the median wage rate and the wage rates for Green List Tier 2 occupations (Appendix 13) with remuneration requirements in effect across time is set out under SR5.15.1.
Note: Where remuneration requirements apply, work in New Zealand will not stop being counted if the specified hourly rate in immigration instructions increases as long as the applicant’s income does not decrease and they have not changed employment.
For example, a crane operator must be paid an hourly rate of 1.3 times the median wage. An applicant can start counting work experience from 29 September 2021 if they earn $35.10 an hour (1.3 times the median wage in effect at the time). When the wage requirement increases to $35.96 an hour on 4 July 2022, they can keep counting their work if they are still in the same job earning $35.10 an hour.
- Despite (f) and (g) above, where an occupation does not have remuneration requirements, applicants who hold or held a visa that was applied for before 29 September 2023 are not required to be paid at or above the median wage for any work in New Zealand gained on and after 29 September 2021 for the period they spent holding a visa described in (c) above.
- For the purposes of these instructions, any leave consistent with the definition in section 16 of the Holidays Act 2003 (including parental leave and ACC leave) taken during a period of work in New Zealand in a Tier 2 Green List role can be counted.
- Despite (a) above, where an occupation is removed from the Tier 2 Green List after the applicant has started to count work in New Zealand towards the 24 months required, the work can continue to be counted if:
- the applicant remains in the occupation; and
- continues to meet the requirements of the Green List as they were listed for the duration of the 24 month period.
- If an applicant has worked in New Zealand for at least 24 months in the last 30 month period but has not maintained a role in a Green List Tier 2 occupation for the full 24 months, they can still been considered for the grant of residence if they meet the requirements set out for work in New Zealand earning at least twice the median wage (see SR5.20) for the balance of the 24 months.
Note: The 24 months of work in New Zealand does not have to be gained consecutively and can be a total of different periods, for example two 12-month periods with a gap of six months between. Additionally, it can be made up of different types of work in New Zealand, for example 18 months in a Tier 2 Green List role and six months in a role paid twice the median wage.

- hold a work visa or a critical purpose visitor visa with work conditions at the time the residence application is made; and
- meet acceptable employment requirements in a Tier 2 Green List occupation (see SR5.10); and
- have completed 24 months of work in New Zealand in a Tier 2 Green List occupation (see SR5.15); and
- meet the relevant wage rate in effect at the time:
- they began to accrue skilled work experience in New Zealand that counts towards their residence requirements; or
- their work visa, was granted if it was granted in the five months before the applicant began to accrue their skilled work experience in New Zealand; and
- be aged 55 or younger at the time the residence application is made.
- An applicant may be considered to meet the relevant wage rate when they apply for residence if they meet the rate for their occupation in effect on the applicable date specified in (b)(iv) above.
- For the purpose of these instructions, applicants must accrue 24 months of skilled work experience in New Zealand within the 30 months immediately prior to submitting their residence application.
Note: For the purposes of determining whether skilled work experience has been completed within the 30-month period, this period is calculated backwards from the date the resident visa is submitted.
Example:
A loader operator began their skilled work experience on 3 March 2026 with a remuneration of 1.15x the median wage ($38.59 per hour at that time). When they apply for residence on 3 September 2028, they need to have accrued 24 months of skilled work experience in the 30-month period immediately before (i.e. in the period from 3 March 2026 to 3 September 2028). The pay rate that they need to meet when they apply for residence is the rate that applied when they began to accrue their work experience, i.e. $38.59 per hour.
Example:
-An applicant has their work visa approved on 14 November 2025, for an occupation which must be paid at least the median wage. The median wage at that time was $33.56 per hour.
-They began their skilled work experience on 12 March 2026 in a role paying $34.00 per hour when the median wage had increased to $35.00.
-However, as less than five months had passed between the date of work visa approval and the commencement of their skilled employment, they are considered to meet the relevant wage rate for that occupation as long as they maintain at or above the median wage in effect on 14 November 2025 and submit an application for residence by 12 September 2028. If maintained, this wage rate ($33.56 per hour) is the wage rate that applies at the time of the residence application.
-(This assumes the 30 month period immediately before applying for residence is 12 March 2026 – 12 September 2028).
- Applications must be made using the approved online form provided on the Immigration New Zealand website.

nz-inz-opsmanual:WA4.10.10@2022-07-04.body:
- A person may hold Accredited Employer work visas based on employment paid below the median wage (WA3.15(b)) for a maximum period of 2 years before they are subject to a stand-down period.
- A person subject to a stand-down period is not eligible for a further Accredited Employer work visa based on employment paid below the median wage until they have spent 12 consecutive months outside New Zealand.
- Applicants who have spent 12 consecutive months outside New Zealand are no longer subject to a stand-down period (the maximum period referred to in (a) begins again) and may be granted further Accredited Employer work visas for the duration allowed by WA4.15.

nz-inz-opsmanual:WA4.10.20@2024-04-07.body:
- An application for an Accredited Employer work visa can be granted if it is made on the basis of a previously used Job Check number, provided the applicant holds an Accredited Employer work visa and that application:
- was made on the basis of that Job Check number; and
- was either submitted:
- between 21 June 2023 and 6 April 2024 (inclusive) and their current Accredited Employer work visa was granted based on employment assessed as paid at or above the median wage; or
- before 21 June 2023 and their current Accredited Employer work visa was granted based on employment assessed as paid at or above the median wage and granted based on an occupation assessed as:
- ANZSCO skill level 1, 2, or 3; or
- on the Green List (Appendix 13); or
- included in the Transport Sector: Work to Residence (SR7) as of 6 April 2024; or
- being paid at or above 1.5 times median wage; or
- on or before 6 April 2024 and were granted based on an occupation included in the Care workforce or Transport sector agreements (Appendix 14).
Note: For the purposes of WA4.10.20 median wage refers to the median wage in place at the time the applicant’s current visa was applied for.
- A subsequent Accredited Employer work visa may only be granted under these instructions if the offer of employment is made by an accredited employer and the following details of the employment offered in the current application are the same as the conditions of employment upon which the applicant’s current Accredited Employer work visa was based:
- the location of the job; and
- the occupation; and
- the remuneration (the remuneration must be no less than the remuneration offered at the time their current visa was granted); and
- the direct employer (as defined at WA2.60.5).
Note: Subsequent Accredited Employer work visa applications applied for using a re-used Job Check number as per WA4.10.20, must meet the requirements at WA4 at the time of the application.

nz-inz-opsmanual:WA4.10.20@2025-09-29.body:
- A subsequent application for an Accredited Employer work visa (AEWV) from an AEWV holder can be granted if it is made on the basis of the job token they most recently used (whether the job token was used for an AEWV application or for a Job Change application) and if the application for the AEWV the applicant currently holds was made on or before 9 March 2025.
- Despite (a), a subsequent application for an AEWV made on the basis of the most recently used Job Check number cannot be granted where the application for the AEWV the applicant currently holds was for one of the following occupations and where the rate of pay was below $29.66:
- Meat process worker (831311)
- Seafood process worker (831313)
- Snowsport Instructor (452314)
- Mountain or Glacier Guide (452214)
- Snow Groomer (721999)

- Outdoor Adventure Guides nec (452299)
- Whitewater Rafting Guide (452217)
- Parachute Rigger (399999)
- Ski Technician (399999)

- A subsequent Accredited Employer work visa may only be granted under these instructions if the offer of employment is made by an accredited employer and the following details of the employment offered in the current application are the same as the conditions of employment upon which the applicant’s current Accredited Employer work visa was based:
- the location of the job; and
- the occupation; and
- the remuneration (the remuneration must be no less than the remuneration specified in the conditions); and

nz-inz-opsmanual:WA4.10.6@2024-09-22.body:
- An applicant meets the minimum skills threshold if an immigration officer is satisfied that they:
- can demonstrate three years or more of relevant work experience with sufficient evidence from a third party; or
- have a relevant qualification at Level 4 or higher on the New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework (NZQCF).
- A qualification or work experience can be considered to be relevant if it is in the same field or industry as the job offered.
- Qualifications that are Bachelor’s degrees or higher can be considered relevant to any employment offered.
- Evidence of relevant work experience from a third party may include, but is not limited to:
- letters of reference from an employer; or
- certificates of employment; or
- payslips; or
- tax certificates.
Note: For the avoidance of doubt, a curriculum vitae is not sufficient unless it is provided with supporting documentation not written by the applicant that satisfies an immigration officer.
- Evidence of a qualification at Level 4 or higher on the NZQCF must include:
- a copy of the qualification certificate awarded to the applicant specifying the qualification type and awarding institution; and
- an NZQA assessment (International Qualification Assessment (IQA)) provided with the application, if the qualification was gained outside of New Zealand and is not a Level 7 Bachelor’s degree or higher.
- Despite WA4.10.6(a), an applicant can be considered to meet the minimum skills threshold if:
- the employment offered is for an occupation that is on the Green List and they meet the current requirements on the list for that occupation (Appendix 13); or
- the employment offered has a proposed remuneration of twice the median wage or higher.
- An immigration officer may accept that the applicant meets the minimum skills threshold, without the applicant providing evidence, where:
- an immigration officer has already assessed and accepted them as part of a previous application; or
- the applicant holds evidence of full or provisional occupational registration for the job they have been offered, where the specifications were required to obtain that registration.
- To protect animal welfare in the 2024 calving season, an applicant who is in New Zealand on 2 August 2024 is exempt from meeting the minimum skills threshold if their application was submitted between 7 April 2024 and 2 August 2024 (inclusive) and is a Dairy Cattle Farm Worker (ANZSCO code 841512).
- An applicant is exempt from meeting the minimum skills threshold if an immigration officer is satisfied that their occupation is listed under Appendix 14 of the Operational Manual (exemptions to the median wage threshold) and:
- employment has been offered under the 2024/25 season (31 August 2024 to 31 August 2025) of the capped meat processing sector agreement (WA3.15.5(a)(i)); or
- employment has been offered under the 2024/25 season (31 October 2024 to 31 October 2025) of the capped seafood processing sector agreement (WA3.15.5(a)(ii)); or
- the applicant holds a valid Accredited Employer work visa under the tourism and hospitality wage exemption that expires on or before 31 March 2025 and is applying for a further visa for the same role; or
- the applicant holds a valid Accredited Employer work visa under the care workforce sector agreement that was granted between 4 July 2022 and 23 November 2023 (inclusive) in a role that was paid at least $26.16 per hour and is applying for a further one-year duration visa for the same role.
Note: For the purpose of the instructions under WA4.10.6 (iii) and (iv), employment in the ‘same role’ allows for employment with a different employer and/or in a different location.
nz-inz-opsmanual:WA4.10.6@2024-09-22.heading: WA4.10 Determining an Accredited Employer work visa / WA4.10.6 Determining whether an applicant meets the minimum skills threshold

nz-inz-opsmanual:WA4.10.7@2024-09-22.body:
- An Accredited Employer work visa must be declined if the maximum continuous stay period holding an Accredited Employer work visa has been met.
- The maximum continuous stay period depends on when the applicant’s first Accredited Employer work visa application was submitted and whether the role is paid at or above the median wage.
- If the applicant’s current offer of employment is paid at or above the median wage (currently $29.66), and the first Accredited Employer work visa application was submitted between 21 June 2023 and 6 April 2024 (inclusive) for a role paid
- at or above median wage, the applicant is eligible for a maximum continuous stay holding an Accredited Employer work visa of 5 years; or
- below median wage, the applicant is eligible for a maximum continuous stay as outlined in table (d) below.
- If the applicant’s current offer of employment is paid at or above the median wage (currently $29.66), and the first Accredited Employer work visa application was submitted on or before 20 June 2023 or on or after 7 April 2024, the applicant is eligible for a maximum continuous stay as outlined in the table below.
| Current offer of employment assessed as | Maximum Continuous Stay
| i. ANZSCO Skill Level 1, 2, or 3; or | 60 months (5 years)
| ii. on the Green List (Appendix 13); or
| iii. included in the Transport Sector: Work to Residence (SR7); or
| iv. included in the Transport Sector: Work to Residence (SR7) as of 6 April 2024 and they hold an AEWV that was submitted on or before 6 April 2024; or
| v. paid at or above 1.5 times the median wage in the Skilled Migrant Category (SR3.10(b) (currently $47.41 per hour)); or
| vi. ANZSCO Skill Level 4 or 5 (where the employment is not otherwise assessed as meeting (d)(i) to (v) above) | 36 months (3 years)
- If the current offer of employment is for an occupation in the care workforce sector (Appendix 14) and is paid at or above median wage ($29.66), the applicant is eligible for a maximum continuous stay of 5 years.
- If the current offer of employment is paid below the median wage ($29.66), the applicant is eligible for a maximum continuous stay as set out in WA4.10.10.
- Where the applicant has already held a visa in line with the maximum continuous stay periods outlined in (c), (d), (e) and (f) above without spending the required time outside New Zealand (as set out at (i) below) the maximum continuous stay period has been met and the Accredited Employer work visa must be declined.
- Where an applicant is outside of New Zealand when the visa is granted, the maximum continuous stay period must be counted from the first date of entry to New Zealand after the grant of the visa.
- The required time outside New Zealand is:
- 12 consecutive months; or
- the time specified in WA4.10.10 if the role is paid below the median wage ($29.66).
- A person who has spent the required time outside New Zealand can be granted a further Accredited Employer work visa for the duration allowed by WA4.15. Once they reach the maximum continuous stay period again, they must once again spend the required time outside of New Zealand.
Notes:
- The median wage rate of $29.66 for the Accredited Employer Work Visa and the maximum continuous stay reflects the June 2022 quarter publication of median wage data by Statistics New Zealand.
- The ‘required time spent outside of New Zealand’ is the duration a person is required to be outside of New Zealand to be eligible for a further Accredited Employer work visa. A person may remain in New Zealand and hold another type of visa (e.g a visitor visa or a Working Holiday visa) however this will not count towards the time spent outside of New Zealand.
- The maximum continuous stay period excludes any time spent on an interim visa between Accredited Employer work visas or any other temporary or work visa (i.e. a student or visitor visa, or Essential Skills work visa).

nz-inz-opsmanual:WA4.10@2022-07-04.body:
- An immigration officer may grant an Accredited Employer work visa if they are satisfied that the applicant:
- meets the generic work visa requirements for applicants at W2.10.1; and
- holds an offer of employment that meets the requirements at WA4.10.1; and
- is suitably qualified by training and experience to do the job they have been offered, as set out at WA4.10.5; and
- where the employment is paid below the median wage (WA3.15(b)), is not subject to the stand-down period as set out at WA4.10.10; and
- has a Job Check number (a number referring to a job that has been approved as part of a Job Check application) that has not been used to approve another Accredited Employer work visa application.
- If there is information that indicates the employer may no longer meet the requirements of their accreditation, an immigration officer may postpone making a decision on the application until the employer is determined to meet the requirements, or until the employer’s accreditation is revoked (WA2.55).
- If the employer’s accreditation is suspended, an immigration officer may postpone making a decision on the application until the suspension ends.
- If the employer’s accreditation expires or is revoked, an immigration officer may decline the application.
- Applicants who hold a work visa with remuneration as a condition of that visa, may be required to provide evidence of their remuneration payment, such as an Inland Revenue income summary and bank statements.
nz-inz-opsmanual:WA4.10@2022-07-04.heading: WA4.10 Determining an Accredited Employer work visa

nz-inz-opsmanual:WA4.10@2026-06-01.body:
- An immigration officer may grant an Accredited Employer work visa if they are satisfied that the applicant:
- meets the generic work visa requirements for applicants at W2.10.1; and
- holds an offer of employment that meets the requirements at WA4.10.1; and
- is suitably qualified by training and experience to do the job they have been offered, as set out at WA4.10.5 and meet the minimum skills threshold as set out at WA4.10.6; and
- has not exceeded a maximum continuous stay period as set out at WA4.11.1; and
- has a job token that has not been used to approve another Accredited Employer work visa application, unless that work visa has been varied to allow the visa holder to work for a different employer or the job token has been reused as set out at WA4.10.20; and
- meets a minimum standard of English language at WA4.12 for roles assessed at the Job Check as ANZSCO or NOL level 3, 4 or 5, unless the application is for a Global Workforce Seasonal Visa or a Peak Seasonal Visa.
- If there is information that indicates the employer may no longer meet the requirements of their accreditation, an immigration officer may postpone making a decision on the application until the employer is determined to meet the requirements, or until the employer’s accreditation is revoked (WA2.55).
- If the employer’s accreditation is suspended, an immigration officer may postpone making a decision on the application until the suspension ends.
- If the employer’s accreditation expires or is revoked, an immigration officer may decline the application.
- Applicants who hold a work visa with remuneration as a condition of that visa, may be required to provide evidence of their remuneration payment, such as an Inland Revenue income summary and bank statements.
- If the application is for a Global Workforce Seasonal Visa or a Peak Seasonal Visa, an immigration officer must be satisfied that the applicant meets:
- the requirements for an Accredited Employer work visa set out at WA4.10(a) to (e) above; and
- any requirements that are specific to the relevant seasonal visa applied for, including any specific requirements for:
- employment offered (WA4.10.1); and
- the applicant to be suitably qualified (WA4.10.5) where relevant; and
- the minimum skills threshold (WA4.10.6); and
- the maximum continuous stay period (WA4.11.2); and
- health and character (WA4.13.1); and
- medical insurance (WA4.13.2) where relevant.
